title: Grok-4.6 reference-tier auto-corroboration floods intake
body:
`derivePromotion` in `src/qa/ticket.ts` marks a cluster `corroborated` as soon as `evidence.tiers` includes `"reference"`:

```
if (evidence.tiers.includes("reference")) return "corroborated";
if (evidence.families.length >= 2) return "corroborated";
```

That is the intended calibration-instrument rule (a few expensive players checking the cheap cohort). It is the wrong rule for a **100-player Grok 4.6 (low) instant-thinking wave**.

`blind-tester/catalogs/grok_cli.json` stamps `grok-4.6` `tier: "reference"` with `settings.reasoning_effort: "low"`. The dedicated lane `npm run playtest:grok-wave` pins that model and effort and fans out up to 32 OS children. A dry-run of `bin/triage.ts` against `ai-runs/playtest/sessions-grok-stress-20260901` (100 sessions, 92 interviews) produced **525 issues → 392 clusters, all corroborated, 392 actionable**. Same family, one wave, slightly different wording — the clusterer barely merged them.

`isActionable` then lets every one of those cross into `intake/queue/`. `intake/queue` is the **short working board**; `qa/tickets/` is the **idle shelf**. This leak would flood both.

**Fix (do not do in this ticket's landing):** treat the cheap Grok-4.6 instant-thinking wave as **volume**, not reference — either retier the catalog entry the wave actually pins, or stop letting single-family reference presence auto-corroborate a mass cohort. Reference-tier corroboration was bought for a small expensive check, not 100 low-effort Grok runs.

Do **not** dump the 392 clusters into intake. A handful of ranked P0/P1 items belong on the working board; the rest stay in `qa/tickets/`.
